newsitem.title: FRANCE: African immigrants occupy UNESCO Paris offices.
newsitem.headline: African immigrants occupy UNESCO Paris offices.

text.p: Up to 50 illegal African immigrants briefly occupied UNESCO's Paris headquarters on Friday to demand residence papers from the French government, officials of the United Nations agency said.

The immigrants, part of a group that occupied a Paris church for two months this summer in protest at France's strict immigration laws, left the building without incident after about six hours when UNESCO agreed to further talks on their plight.

"Today we ask UNESCO to make its voice heard in response to our arbitrary treatment by the government," the immigrants said in a statement. French riot police were sent to the scene but were not called into service.

The Africans had asked to send a delegation of three to UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation) offices to discuss their cause but 40 to 50 showed up, officials said.
In August, police stormed the Saint Bernard church in Paris, evicting some 300 African immigrants including 10 on a 50-day hunger strike seeking to obtain residence papers.
About half succeeded but the other half still needed the papers to remain in France, according to the protesters' statement.
